mechanism_finding_precise.detail: Review §D's predicted mechanism requires TWO resolution entries to exist side-by-side after `_emit_spec_matches` runs: (1) the customer's ORIGINAL per-token resolution, left with `matches:[]` + its trgm `alternatives` untouched, and (2) a NEW resolution keyed on `payload.query` (the restated string) carrying the spec matches -- with `_tokenWasAnswered` then failing entry (1) against `_answerCodes` built from entry (2)'s uuids, producing a leaked did-you-mean under the spec answer. Directly observed here: `resolutions` has exactly ONE entry total, keyed on the restated string, with the spec matches. There is no second entry for the raw token 'wall hung basin' at all -- not even one carrying `matches:[]`. §D's two-entry precondition is simply absent for a SINGLE-TOKEN AND query: resolutions is sized to the token count (1 token in, 1 slot total), so there is no separate slot for a leftover to occupy in the first place.
mechanism_finding_precise.contrast_with_SA4_SA5: SA-4 ('wall hung basin got SIRIM cert?') and SA-5 ('SRTWC286 and wall hung basin') ARE multi-token queries, and in both, 'wall hung basin' DOES get its own independent resolution entry (matches:[], alternatives: 3 trgm codes) sitting alongside a SIBLING token's entry -- the exact shape §D's mechanism needs a leftover to occupy. But in those two cases the widened arm never engaged for the 'wall hung basin' token at all (per the rollup's review_corrections_20260812 note: 'SA-4/SA-5 floor-missed on the widened arm') -- no spec rows appeared, so there was nothing for '_tokenWasAnswered' to fail against. Neither of the three n8n-level runs I have (SA-4, SA-5, SA-7) sits at the intersection §D actually worries about: a MULTI-TOKEN query where the widened arm fires for one token above the ranker floor while a SIBLING token's own resolution survives unanswered alongside it.
